question: As per Sample Registration System 2020, what is the infant death rate in India?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**28 per thousand live births**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **infant mortality rate (IMR)** is defined as the number of deaths of children under the age of one year per thousand live births.
 
• According to the **Sample Registration System (SRS) 2020**, India's infant mortality rate has been recorded as **28 per thousand live births**.
 
• This figure shows significant improvement over the years, reflecting the success of various **government initiatives** and health programs aimed at reducing infant mortality.
 
• Programs such as the **National Rural Health Mission (NRHM)** and **Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health (RMNCH+A)** have played a crucial role in addressing infant and maternal health issues.
 
• The reduction in IMR indicates better access to **healthcare facilities, immunization, nutrition, and sanitation** across the country.
 
• States like **Kerala** and **Tamil Nadu** have performed exceptionally well in reducing IMR due to their focus on public healthcare systems.
 
• However, some states still have higher IMR, which highlights the need for targeted efforts in regions with poor healthcare infrastructure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **31 per thousand live births**__

 __
 
• This figure represents a slightly older estimate of infant mortality rate (IMR) in India, indicating progress has been made in reducing infant deaths.
 
 
 
• **19 per thousand live births**__
 __
 
• This rate is much lower and represents the IMR of some states like **Kerala**, which are known for their advanced healthcare systems.
 
 
 
• **44 per thousand live births**__
 
 
• This was an older statistic from previous years, showcasing India's past challenges in reducing infant mortality rates.
